$comment: THE CLAIMS LEDGER — every number the site prints, with its basis.
A figure on a page is marked with the entry it is:
164
by hand on the hand-authored pages (index.html, carbon-ai.html,
field-report.html, 404.html), and by npm run build:content wherever a
generated page prints one from content/ (scripts/lib/claims.js finds it
by its value or one of its `forms`). claims.html, 'Check my numbers', is
built from this file: each figure, where it appears, its basis and
whether a reader can check it. tests/claims.test.js fails the build on a
marked figure that disagrees with its entry, an unknown id, an entry
with no basis, a numeral on any page that is neither marked nor a year,
a date, a section number, a standard's name and the like, and a number
the narration says aloud that no entry here backs.
FIELDS (scripts/lib/content.js refuses anything else)
id         kebab-case; the mark on the page
value      the figure as the site writes it: "164", "70%", "2–8×"
unit       what it counts or measures, as claims.html says it after the
value; no other figure in it
forms      optional; other ways the generated pages write it ("~276")
spoken     optional; how the narration says it, in words, with what
follows ("a hundred and sixty-four water points")
basis      exactly one of
result        a case study's id: one of its results states
the figure, and its basis and checkability
are this entry's (not repeated here)
profile       a path, or paths, in content/profile.json
("experience.4.teamSize"); a note when the
figure is counted from it rather than read
factor        a path in ai-carbon-data.js: a calculator's
input, with its cited source
source        a cited external source, with its url
budget        a budget scripts/check-budget.js measures
derived       worked out from other entries (`from`)
illustrative  why it has no source; it must say
'illustrative' wherever it is shown
and a `note` where a reader needs one. No figure in a note
unless it is an entry here.
checkable  public (a reader can check it from outside: `check` says
where), on-request (the evidence is a document Moses holds),
or not-checkable (it rests on records held elsewhere). A
result's comes from the case study.
Numbers the calculators work out in the browser (AI, Weighed, the
homepage chart, the footer's receipt) are model outputs, not claims:
their inputs are entries here, where the pages print them, and every
factor is in the evidence ledger on carbon-ai.html. The open counts on
stats.html are the visit counter's own measurements, rewritten weekly.
